# How to use this Ignition Project

## Purpose
* Ignition is great at connecting data from one area of the plant to another. It can also make API calls to other services if there is a valid internet connection. 
* Because Ignition is usually placed at the center of the OT network, it usually has great visibility to all devices in the plant, including label printers. 
* Additionally, it is natural for labels to be printed on a trigger after a certain PLC event occurs, and using Ignition allows fine-tuned control over these processes.
* This makes Ignition an incredible tool for integrating databases with label printers. It can store label templates using ZPL code and populate it dynamically with different pieces of information based on the item to be labeled.

## Helpful Software
* [ZPL Programming Manual](https://docs.zebra.com/us/en/printers/software/zpl-pg/zpl-ii,-zbi-2,-set-get-do,-mirror,-wml-programming-guide.html), or [Labelary ZPL Intro](https://labelary.com/zpl.html), for learning ZPL code.
* [Labelary Docs](https://labelary.com/docs.html), for using the Labelary API and understanding which ZPL commands are supported on the API.
*  [ZebraDesigner3](https://www.zebra.com/us/en/support-downloads/software/printer-software/zebra-designer-3-downloads.html?downloadId=81ad3292-7f21-4dca-bd86-2535cb5c066f) (ZD3), for designing labels in a GUI before importing to this Ignition tool.
* [Zebra Printer Setup Utilities](https://www.zebra.com/us/en/support-downloads/software/printer-software/printer-setup-utilities.html), required for ZebraDesigner3 (pick a 203 dpi printer model like "ZT621 203 dpi ZPL" to install the drivers in Windows)
* [Porrey's Virtual ZPL Printer](https://github.com/porrey/Virtual-ZPL-Printer), or [DChupp's Printer Emulator](https://github.com/dchupp/printerEmulator), for testing the print feature without a physical label printer
* [Porrey's Virtual ZPL Printer Setup Instructions on Windows](https://github.com/porrey/Virtual-ZPL-Printer/discussions/39) (redundant driver if installing Zebra Printer Setup Utilities)

## Ignition Project Info
* This ignition project follows the naming conventions defined in the [Ignition Exchange Style Guide](https://inductiveautomation.com/exchange/about), and it can be used as a standalone application or imported into another project (any project folders named "exchange").
* It is intended to be paired with a PostgreSQL database connection named "ex_zpl_label_printing" on the Ignition gateway config page. This name is critical since a lot of scripts rely on the system.db.runPrepQuery system functions. The PostgreSQL schema name is also changed from "public" to "ex_zpl_label_printing".
* The folder "Tag Based Printer Settings" is optional and contains an example for using UDTs to manage the printer settings instead of the database connection if preferred. 
* Custom python libraries imported inside scripts include "socket" (http connections), "re" (regex), "Base64 (java.util)" (image encoding), "os" (for ping on Windows, Linux, and OS X), the ancient "java.awt" library, and the Labelary API.
* This project can be run in any version of Ignition 8.1.0+, but 8.1.22 is required for the advanced CSS stylesheet to be enabled (this is only used for a fancy page zoom function on the header)
* The project is based on the default Web Navigation 8.1 Template project and the only extra resources are the "Exchange" folders inside of Scripting, Perspective Views, and Named Queries. 

## Using this Tool

### Printer Settings
* Printer settings are stored in the Postgres database. Each printer has a name, IP Address, and offset values in millimeters for the x and y directions.
* The offsets are used in case the physical label printer is physically misaligned compared to the Labelary preview. 
* If the printer name matches any printer that already exists in the database, it updates that printer's settings.
* If there is no match in printer names, it adds it as a new record in the database. 
* To remove a printer from the database, select a row and click the "Delete" button.

### Manage Users
* This functionality does not do much in this Exchange Resource, but it is included with the database schema to allow different label templates to be assigned to different users. 
* To illustrate a few examples of where this functionality could be extended, the "User" can be a person, or a Customer with specific label specs different than other customers, or a machine that prints a different size label. 
* The usage of this page is simple. First select a Label Template. Then add or delete users from that Label Template (there is no update, since this page is simplistic). 

### Edit Labels 
* This page is for editing existing label templates in SQL, deleting them, or adding new ones. 
* First select <New\> or an existing template from the dropdown menu. 
* If an existing template is selected, the "Delete" and "Update" buttons are visible at the bottom left. Edit the text in the text area component and click Preview at any time while editing to see the updated image. Then click "Update" to save the changes.
* If the word <New\> is selected, the File Upload component will allow 1 file to be uploaded (instead of 0). The New Label Name text box will also appear at the bottom left. Design a label in Zebra Designer 3, print to file, and then upload the .prn file to place the zpl text in the text area. Make any adjustments as necessary, and click the "Add" button to add the record to SQL. 

### Print Labels
* This page is for printing labels. Either select an existing template or type in ZPL code manually into the text area component. 
* If selecting a label template with the word "parameter" or "parameterized" in the name, the text area will change into a list of parameters. This will be a list of anything surrounded by [brackets\] in the ZPL string for the label template.
* After changing any of the text in the text area or parameter values, click the "Preview" button to update the zpl string on the Image component before printing.
* Next, select the printer, the number of copies (qty) to print, and adjust the offsets. 
* Finally, click the "Print" button to print to the selected printer. Cancel the print job at any time. 

## Local Print Preview Supported ZPL Commands (failover if no Labelary connection)
* Most global commands like ^FW and ^CF are not supported. All ZPL lines must start with either ^FT or ^FO, (followed by ^Afo,h,w for any text)
* [^POa](https://docs.zebra.com/us/en/printers/software/zpl-pg/c-zpl-zpl-commands/r-zpl-po.html) Print Orientation, where valid values are N (Normal) or I (Inverted or rotated 180 degrees)
* [^FTx,y,z](https://docs.zebra.com/us/en/printers/software/zpl-pg/c-zpl-zpl-commands/r-zpl-ft.html) Field Typeset, where x,y position is the bottom left corner of the field rectangle, and z is 0 for left-justify and 1 for right-justify
* [^FOx,y,z](https://docs.zebra.com/us/en/printers/software/zpl-pg/c-zpl-zpl-commands/r-zpl-fo.html) Field Origin, where x,y position is the top left corner of the field rectangle, and z is 0 for left-justify and 1 for right-justify
* [^Afo,h,w](https://docs.zebra.com/us/en/printers/software/zpl-pg/c-zpl-zpl-commands/r-zpl-a.html) Font for field, with options for font name, orientation, height, and width (stretch factor)
  * only f = '0' (zebra default) and f = 'A' (zebra monospace) fonts are supported
* [^FDa](https://docs.zebra.com/us/en/printers/software/zpl-pg/c-zpl-zpl-commands/r-zpl-fd.html) Field Data string and  [^FS](https://docs.zebra.com/us/en/printers/software/zpl-pg/c-zpl-zpl-commands/r-zpl-fs.html) End of Field Definition
* [^FBa,b,c,d,e](https://docs.zebra.com/us/en/printers/software/zpl-pg/c-zpl-zpl-commands/r-zpl-fb.html) Field Block with length in dots and row count. Uses automatic word wrap; however, the "Arial Narrow" font used in place of the Zebra0 font is slightly narrower, so be wary that too much text can overflow on the physical label but will not show in the preview.
* [^GBw,h,t,c,r](https://docs.zebra.com/us/en/printers/software/zpl-pg/c-zpl-zpl-commands/r-zpl-gb.html) Graphic Box, where you can define width, height, stroke thickness, line color (B or W), and degree of corner rounding (0 to 8, where 8 has diameter = shortest side length)
* [^GFa,b,c,d,data](https://docs.zebra.com/us/en/printers/software/zpl-pg/c-zpl-zpl-commands/r-zpl-gf.html) Graphic Field or Image data encoded in base64. Only a 100x100 dot black square, containing the text "imagePlaceholder" is used to represent an image. Additionally it may be out of position. Treated as a QR code (^BQ command)
* [^BYw,r,h](https://docs.zebra.com/us/en/printers/software/zpl-pg/c-zpl-zpl-commands/r-zpl-by.html) Barcode Field Defaults, which are used to define barcode width scale factor, wide to narrow bar ratio, and barcode height.
* [^BCo,h,f,g,e,m](https://docs.zebra.com/us/en/printers/software/zpl-pg/c-zpl-zpl-commands/r-zpl-bc.html) Code 128 barcodes and other 1D barcodes (^B* commands), represented by a black rectangle with white text for what is encoded within the barcode. Height and positions of barcodes (without interpretation lines) should be correct. However, the barcode length is difficult to calculate without a barcode library, and so it is inaccurate.
* [^BQa,b,c,d,e](https://docs.zebra.com/us/en/printers/software/zpl-pg/c-zpl-zpl-commands/r-zpl-bq.html) QR code and other 2D barcodes or multi-row 1D barcodes (^B* commands), represented by a 100x100 dot black square with white text for what is encoded in the barcode. It may be slightly out of position and poorly sized, but aims to show a placeholder for the barcode on the label.


## Other Notes on ZPL, Printer Time, and Zebra Designer:
* In Zebra Designer Document Properties, the orientation can be set to "Landscape" with "Rotated" left unchecked.
* ^SL0,1 a command that configures the real-time clock on the printer so that each label prints with the timestamp that it was printed. 
* ^FC%,{,#^FD%H:%M^FS will print the timestamp in HH:mm format (24-hour time). %m/%d/%Y will print in MM/DD/YYYY format, while %y%m%d will print in YYMMDD format. 
* ^LT0 is offset dots in x direction and ^LS0 is offset dots in y direction when rotated 90 or 270 degrees (landscape labels). (but for portrait labels ^LT0 is up/down and ^LS0 is left/right). 
* Note that the Labelary API png image will show UTC time, but the printer will print local time according to its own timeclock or time server.
* If the time of printing is required, it can be added in Zebra Designer 3 with this method: 
  1. Add a text field to the label.
  2. On the "Source" tab, select "Current time" under the "Data" dropdown. 
  3. Select "Output format:" to be "h24:mm"
  4. Then click "Advanced properties"
  5. Go to the "Output rules" tab, and then modify the "Prefix" or "Suffix" fields as necessary.
